thread:
maria (support): FYI customer on Private/VPC reporting intermittent 502s and TLS failures only when their requests go through corporate proxy. Works fine from home. Customer says proxy is 'transparent' but might be doing TLS inspection. Sample repro they ran below.

sam (net): Can you paste the raw CONNECT exchange / tcpdump? If the proxy terminates TLS or strips SNI we'll see it in the ClientHello. Also need vendor/version for their proxy.

maria (support): Customer curl output (sanitized):

`curl --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 -v https://private-api.redwood.internal/generate`

```
* Connected to corp-proxy (10.10.20.5) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT private-api.redwood.internal:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: private-api.redwood.internal:443
> Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* Proxy replied OK to CONNECT request
* TLS handshake start
* error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
* Closing connection 0
```

maria (support): tcpdump excerpt the customer provided (trimmed):

```
10:23:12.345678 IP client.50123 > corp-proxy.8080: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
10:23:12.345999 IP corp-proxy.8080 > client.50123: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
10:23:12.346100 IP client.50123 > corp-proxy.8080: CONNECT private-api.redwood.internal:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: private-api.redwood.internal\r\n\r\n
10:23:12.346200 IP corp-proxy.52000 > private-api.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240   <-- proxy opens separate TCP session
10:23:12.346300 IP private-api.443 > corp-proxy.52000: Flags [.] ack 1
10:23:12.346400 IP corp-proxy.52000 > private-api.443: [no TLS ClientHello observed from proxy]
10:23:12.346500 IP private-api.443 > corp-proxy.52000: RST, ack 1   <-- immediate reset
```

sam (net): That pattern strongly suggests the proxy is doing TLS interception/inspection but not sending a proper TLS ClientHello with SNI to our backend. If it rewrites the SNI to something else (or doesn't include SNI), our cert verification/ALB routing can fail and we get a reset or handshake error.

lee (infra): Also check for header injection on the CONNECT response. Some proxies add/replace Host or X-Forwarded-Host which can confuse our frontends if they assume SNI==host header. Repro step to demonstrate SNI absence: ask customer to run a netcat CONNECT test from inside their network:

```
echo -e "CONNECT private-api.redwood.internal:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: private-api.redwood.internal\r\n\r\n" | nc corp-proxy 8080
```

And then watch whether a TLS ClientHello is forwarded on the proxy->server leg. If you see an immediate TCP teardown after CONNECT 200 that's proxy interception failing.

maria (support): Customer ran that and got `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established` then instant RST from our side. They also tried `openssl s_client` via proxy and got no Server Name extension visible (openssl shows no SNI).

sam (net): Actionable asks for the customer: 1) proxy vendor + version (e.g., BlueCoat, Forcepoint, Zscaler, Squid) 2) proxy policy name for TLS inspection 3) Tcpdump from proxy showing proxy->server leg 4) config snippet if allowed (squid `ssl_bump` / Zscaler passthrough rules).

lee (infra): Mitigations / recommended fixes we can share with customer:
- Enable TLS passthrough for our hostnames (whitelist SNI `private-api.redwood.internal` in the proxy allowlist).
- If the proxy must inspect TLS, configure it to preserve SNI and not rewrite Host headers on CONNECT.
- If proxy uses a custom CA for inspect, ensure the proxy presents a cert chain we can accept or add proxy CA to trusted chain for services that need mTLS (customer-side).
- As a short-term workaround, run the traffic via an egress gateway that does not inspect CONNECTs for our CIDR (whitelist our egress IPs).

maria (support): I'm going to send the exact repro steps + tcpdump snippet to the customer and ask for vendor/version and proxy logs. Also told them to try a quick test: bypass corp proxy from one machine (mobile hotspot) to confirm behaviour.

anya (support): I'll open an internal ticket with escalation label and attach this thread. Also asking Solutions if they want to offer Dedicated lanes or Private config changes for this customer if corporate policy can't be changed.
